newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia rejects plan for U.N. rights bureau.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia rejects plan for U.N. rights bureau.

text.p: State Secretary Murdiono said Indonesia would not approve a plan by the United Nations Human Rights Commission to set up a bureau in Jakarta, newspapers reported on Monday.
Murdiono was quoted by the Republika newspaper as saying the plan would breach Indonesia's sovereignty.
"It is improper to intervene in the problems which are the internal business of a country," he told reporters in Bandung, the capital of West Java.
U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights Jose Ayala-Lasso said last September he was negotiating with Colombia and Indonesia to open monitoring offices in both countries.

The U.N. Human Rights Commission issued a statement last April expressing "deep concern" over alleged human rights violations in East Timor, which Indonesia invaded in 1975 and annexed the following year in a move not recognised by the United Nations.
Murdiono was quoted by the Merdeka newspaper as saying that Indonesia upheld human rights, but that the issue should be treated through the country's own perspective.
He said Indonesia's reserved the right to decide how to handle human rights issues and that it was unwilling to be dictated to by other countries.
He said the United Nations had not formally contacted the Indonesian government on setting up a rights bureau. Merdeka gave no further details.
